items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I played with George. And I really enjoyed it, you know. It was fun.

ctx.x: Who'd you play with this year?

I played with Al Grey and I played with Vic. We played together. And there's another guy up there that plays with the World's Greatest Jazz Band now, George Masso. He's a good trombone player. I played with George. And I really enjoyed it, you know. It was fun. It was a fun thing. It got to cooking up there because they had a lot of good rhythm players up there.
Who else was there this year? I didn't see the Lineup (inaudible)...

items.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: Plus there were so many great players in those days, you know there was Jack Teagarden and Cutty Cutshall and Bill Harris and Jack Jenny and Trummy Young. I mean I had all these great players to listen to.

ctx.x: Eight bars and you knew what you wanted to do. That’s saying something.

It was such a driving force but so musical. And from that point on I got all the Goodman sextet records with Lou and learned all his choruses note for note, which is a great way to start I think. Eventually we all hope that we can be ourselves. And we have something that identifies us. But to begin with, you’ve got to hear something you like and you’ve got to hear a style that you like. Plus there were so many great players in those days, you know there was Jack Teagarden and Cutty Cutshall and Bill Harris and…
